content: Neural tube defects occur in human embryos when there is a disruption in the closure of the neural tube, which typically takes place around the 28th day after fertilization. The global incidence of neural tube defects is approximately 6 in 1,000 live births. Pregnant women who are taking medications for epilepsy are at an increased risk of having a child with a neural tube defect. Additionally, research has demonstrated that women with folic acid deficiencies are also at a higher risk of giving birth to a child with a neural tube defect. However, folic acid deficiency is only one contributing factor. While taking folic acid supplements does not completely eliminate the risk of neural tube defects, it significantly reduces the likelihood of their occurrence. In Canada, the mandatory fortification of certain foods with folic acid has been shown to reduce the incidence of neural tube defects by 46%. Women who are pregnant or who may become pregnant are advised to take daily folic acid supplements unless their dietary intake of this nutrient is already consistently high. Neural tube defects can be identified through various methods, including prenatal screening tests and medical imaging techniques. In many cases, these defects are evident at birth. However, occult neural tube defects may remain undiagnosed until much later in life.
